title: Intersectionality in Conversational AI Safety: How Bayesian Multilevel Models Help Understand Diverse Perceptions of Safety

bias_targets.methodology: Applying Bayesian multilevel models to human safety ratings of chatbot conversations to identify differences in safety perception and annotation across various racial and ethnic rater groups.
Applying Bayesian multilevel models to evaluate how a rater's gender, both independently and intersectionally with other demographics, influences their perception of safety in conversational AI.
Analyzing variations in safety ratings among different rater age cohorts (e.g., Gen Z, Millennials, Gen X+) using Bayesian multilevel models.
Evaluating the impact of raters' educational attainment levels (e.g., high school or below vs. college or beyond) on their safety annotations, particularly interacting with indigenous identities.
Collecting and comparing safety annotations from raters situated in two distinct English-speaking locales (US and India) to control for and observe cultural/regional differences in safety perception.
